title: Introduce declarative cost templates and quant rollup manager
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: teams need a reproducible, auditable way to roll out tenant-level cost defaults (batching, cache, quant profiles) and a safe automated path to merge quantization deltas into serving defaults. This PR introduces two pieces: 1) a small declarative templating system (YAML-based) for unit-econ defaults and prefill/cache/quant presets, and 2) a Quant Rollup Manager that ingests per-tenant quant diffs from experiments and synthesizes safe rollups with traffic gating and unit-econ estimates. The goal is to make default tuning a first-class, reviewable artifact (templates-as-code) and to provide a safe automation path for rolling quantization changes across tenants.

Changes in this PR are intentionally scoped to the econ/ and rwctl areas plus docs and a few infra values. High-level features:
- YAML declarative templates: schema + loader + sample templates. Templates can be validated, dry-run simulated, and applied via rwctl. Templates encode batching defaults, cache policies, quant profile pointers, and a short rationale field for audits.
- Quant Rollup Manager: a service-level component that consumes quant diff reports (from A/B experiments), computes an estimated unit-econ delta, and outputs a proposed rollup package with staged rollout settings. Includes a safety gate that prevents any rollup with predicted latency regression > 8% or cost increase > 12% without a manual override.
- rwctl CLI commands: cost-template apply/validate/dry-run and quant-rollup propose/preview/commit. Dry-run mode produces CSV unit economics estimates per-tenant and an overall rollout plan JSON for ops review.
- Simulation harness: lightweight deterministic simulator for estimating batching and cache effects on token throughput based on synthetic traffic profiles included in testdata.
- Telemetry hooks: adds a few metrics (econ.template.apply.count, quant.rollup.proposed.count, quant.rollup.estimated_delta_pct) and tracing spans around the rollup path.
- Docs + examples: operator-facing docs and two sample templates (startup / steady-state) to help teams onboard.

Checklist:
- [x] Declarative template schema + loader
- [x] CLI surface for apply/validate/dry-run
- [x] Quant Rollup Manager core logic + gating rules
- [x] Unit + integration tests for critical paths
- [x] Basic metrics and tracing
- [x] Docs and sample templates

Related: ENG-1823 tracks the templates-as-code product work; PM-451 is the feature request for rollups. This PR depends on a small follow-up to expose the quant-diff reporting API (separate PR will add an ingress hook that posts diffs to /internal/quant-diffs).

ci_checks: e2e-smoke: pass (initial run flaky, rerun succeeded)
release_notes: Add templates-as-code for cost defaults and a Quant Rollup Manager. Operators can now validate and apply guaranteed dry-run proposals and preview estimated unit-econ deltas. Includes rwctl CLI commands and sample templates for quick onboarding.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids automatic commit of rollups to production; the rollup commit path requires an additional approval flow (follow-up PR will add a lightweight RBAC check and audit event webhook). The quant diff ingress will also arrive in a separate patch to keep review scope focused.
qa_summary: Manual QA: ran smoke on staging cluster with two sample templates and verified telemetry and dry-run CSV outputs. Load: small synthetic trace (1000 requests). No regressions observed beyond a single flaky e2e test that was resolved by retry. Post-merge: ops to monitor econ.template.apply.count and quant.rollup.estimated_delta_pct for first 48h.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: changes are mostly additive and behind rwctl CLI. The safety gate prevents accidental wide rollouts. The follow-up RBAC audit will further reduce operational risk.
migration_instructions: N/A - operators can opt into templates by running 'rwctl cost-template validate <file>' and then 'rwctl cost-template apply --dry-run <file>' before committing.
